118385.overview:
Don't Look Back is a retro styled platform game playable through Adobe Flash and designed by Terry Cavanagh. The game is a modern interpretation of the Orpheus and Eurydice Greek legend.

The game is a combination of two ideas; Cavanagh wished to create a "silly shooter" where the player's actions were "redeemed" after being shown from a different perspective, he also wished to create a game where the gameplay acted as a metaphor of the player's actions.

Critics praised the game's addictiveness and presentation, but had different opinions over the game's high difficulty level.

151021.overview:
Internet's gone!
Ohh ... What is that?
A dinosario.
In an era where the advance of the video game industry seems to be measured by the number of frames per second, the number of polygons displayed on the screen or the width in pixels with names like HD, HD ready, Full HD, Ultra HD, 4k and Retina Display (because the aspect of the 16: 9 screen is very mainstream) it is very difficult to expect that a multi-billion dollar company like Google would go against the trends.

T-Rex Runner, also known as "The only thing left to do when going to the Internet," is a game that has all the global capacity with access to a computer but that has never been given the time for analysis and appreciation.
That is why there is a way of retro-analysis, here I leave the review of T-Rex Runner exclusively for Google Chrome.

Join me to live this sad story.
Let's start talking about the theme of the game. A simple view of a Tyrannosaurus Rex running from left to right that points to blocks as segments of small sizes, groups or groups, while earning points for each meter that it does. but the premise goes far beyond just that.

T-Rex Runner presents a tragic unit in a situation where there is no way to win.

T-Rex Runner represents a sad story based on the primary need of almost every living being (with the exception of the Lemores and the members of My Chemical Romance) to preserve their life against any kind of danger, even when tragic outcome is completely inevitable .

Our hero, Rex, is not running alone because he likes to exercise every morning, he runs terrified. Let's think then, if the character is nothing more and nothing less than the king of the dinosaurs and one of the most powerful carnivores (or scavengers, and no one agrees) of history. What could cause so much terror? The answer is simple: Extinction.

151576.overview: Death Worm is a casual game where you control a Mongolian Death Worm who has to kill humans, cars, etc. in order to grow and survive.

156079.overview: Don't Shit Your Pants is a browser-based text adventure game created by Teddy and Kenny "Rete" Lee for Cellar Door Games. The objective of the game is to use a text prompt to prevent a man standing beside a closed door from defecating inappropriately. It was the first title released by the Lee brothers, receiving positive critical reception.

165543.overview:
Everything changes after a big tornado hits and destroys your farm. Only a single duck egg survives, and you must train this duckling into a racing duck to make enough money to rebuild the farm. There are 3 abilities that need to be mastered: running, flying, and swimming. 
You need to train your duck by playing mini games. You can also collect coins while in training to buy seeds and cool accessories for your duckling. Also keep an eye on the energy status which can be increased by feeding it with seed from the shop. Once your skill levels are high enough, head to the races and win them to earn great prizes. Repeat until you finally win the world championship. Have fun with Duck Life!

199909.overview: DragonFable is a free-to-play, online, browser-based, single-player, fantasy, role-playing game developed by Artix Entertainment and updated on a weekly basis.[3] Players may access locked game content by upgrading to a premium account for a one-time fee.

201574.overview:
Dad 'n Me is a side-scrolling fighting game featuring a purple creature that is dropped off by his dad at a park. In a single level, he needs to beat up all the other kids in the park (including ninjas, basketball and football players, and gangster kids), apparently to prove his worth. The graphics are hand drawn by Dan Paladin and are reminiscent of the art style in games such as Alien Hominid and Castle Crashers.

The keyboard is used to move around along with two keys for light or heavy attacks. These can be combined to create combos, hold and throw enemies, rush and jump, and pick up items such as barrels or lawnmowers to take out opponents. The life meter can be replenished with health kits, the game keeps track of the combo rate and when the rage meter is completely full movement becomes faster and the attacks more fierce.

216049.overview:
Throw dummies to reach the goal, less pain the better!

Full features are:

- 52 levels

- 51 dummy skins to unlock

- Level editor

- High-scores

- A lot of dummy pain

419029.overview:
As indicated by the name, Desktop Tower Defense is a strategy game in the tower defense genre that takes place on a desktop—that being an actual desk, as the background shows a wood surface, the edge of a keyboard, and some loose change among other objects. During each round the player is presented with a blank field that they must populate with a variety of towers, all having unique weapon capabilities.

Some of the weapons include Pellet Towers, which simply fire small pellets; Dart Towers, which of course fire darts; Frost Towers, which can freeze the enemy; and Ink Towers, which fire ink that traps the enemies in place. The enemies in this game are known as creeps, and there are multiple varieties which resemble various microorganisms. All have different abilities—some are more resistant to damage, others move faster, while some can even fly (necessitating the use of "anti-aircraft" towers).

The player's score is calculated based on how many creeps escape to the exit, and how much time is left on the clock when they proceed to the next level (once all creeps are destroyed, the player can either wait out the clock, or click on a button to immediately go to the next level). Destroying creeps earns gold that can be used to buy or upgrade towers. Upgrading towers makes them more powerful, and is necessary to defeat some of the more advanced creeps.

422815.overview:
Day Defender is a strategic shooting Flash game.

In this game, the objective of the player is to protect the beach of Normandy by using weapons and upgrading them.

422816.overview:
In Death vs. Monstars you control a shooting skull that fights massive amounts of enemies. Divided into ten levels, the main objective of each level is to stay alive until you kill a certain amount of enemies or until a period of time passes.

The brief story of the game tells about a giant black square that threatens the world, and Death is the only one that can stop him, and so he journeys to the sky to defeat hoards of minions and ultimately the mysterious boss.

The game is mostly controlled with the mouse. The unique aiming system in the game is that the crosshair constantly drags after the player's character, making aiming a bit tricky at first. Instead of just pointing to the direction you want to shoot at, you need to drag the crosshair so it faces the right direction. In addition to the basic shooting, double-clicking the mouse will cause a "Berserk Time" attack, which shoots in all directions for a brief period of time, and also converts some of the shots of the enemies that are flying towards you into money. The last means of protection in your disposal is Bullet Time which activates for a limited amount of time when you hold the Space Bar.

Money must be collected in order to purchase better weapons and upgrades. The four upgrades are increasing your max health, shorter healing time, longer Berserk Time and faster Berserk charge. You will find yourself playing earlier levels in order to raise enough money to buy the upgrades and surviving later levels.

422817.overview: Lead your kingdom to victory against hordes of zombies, orcs, werewolves and trolls in this Middle Ages sequel of the “Decision” series.

422818.overview:
Dead Zed is a first person shooter flash game developed by 3KG Games and released on February 2, 2012.

In Dead Zed, the player must defend their farm from zombies for a total of 40 days, each day bringing a wave of zombies that gets bigger and stronger as time goes on. The player must kill the zombies with guns from a first person perspective but can also have fellow survivors help them defend the farm. In between the waves of zombies, the player can send their search party out to neighbouring buildings in order to find new weapons and more survivors to bring back to the farm and help defend it.

422819.overview: Decision, is the first game in the Decision series. It was released on March 13, 2012. You play as a survivor in a zombie apocalypse working to reclaim a city.

422820.overview:
Defend Your Castle is a remake of the developers' earlier flash-based online game; also called Defend Your Castle. Though many changes have been made, the story and objective remains the same: defend your castle!

Play is with the Wii Remote only. When people attack your castle, you pick them up and fling them away with the A or B button, or use various offensive spells with the d-pad. As the rounds advance, so will the enemies: more types of enemies will appear, and at a faster rate. Money earned by destroying invaders can be used between levels to fund development of major castle towers, or to increase the "health" of the castle. When playing multiplayer, the one with the highest score in the current round is declared King and gets to decide how the money is spent. Play continues until your castle is taken, but with the ability to save between each round there's the chance to give it another try.

Enemies can also be dropped into a Pit of Conversion to turn them to your side. Though they won't fight directly, you can assign them to one of the castle's towers, each representing a different skill. Stone masons will increase the castle's rate of repair. Archers will pick off incoming invaders. The more mages there are, the more offensive spells will be available and the more quickly they'll recharge. Demolition men... explode.

Unlike its predecessor, the Wii game is made to look as if it's made from everyday household items come to life: Men have crayon-drawn bodies and buttons for heads. Clouds of tissue paper on string move across the sky. One of the spells uses an eraser to erase an opponent. Even the players' cursors are those little hard plastic bread ties.

422821.overview:
The sequel to Dolphin Olympics features smoother gameplay, more tricks, and more stuff to see. Score as many points as possible in 2 minutes by
swimming and flipping your dolphin. Successful jumps build speed, allowing for bigger and better tricks!

The alternate version fixes the corkscrew trick, but has no highscore list.

422823.overview: Demonic Defence is a series of action games developed by Antitude Games. It has 4 games in the series.

422824.overview: Death in Sakkara: An Egyptian Adventure is an Egyptian adventure game. The adventure is based on an original idea by the BBC's history team, and includes comic and character illustration by Joe Berger, and an original musical score composed by Pendle Poucher.

422826.overview:
Dino Run takes you back to prehistorical times and casts you as a little dinosaur trying to survive the impending apocalypse. You must run across mountains and caves, escaping the "wall of doom" and finding your way to the dino sanctuary.

The key element of Dino Run is exploration. The game has super eggs to find and special milestones to achieve, which award you in points and "DNA points". Milestones include a number of eggs you collected, a number of runners/lizards/birds you devoured, "Doom surfing" (running close to the wall of doom for a certain period of time) and more.

The DNA points can be used to improve four stats: speed, acceleration, jumping and strength (used to push boulders that are thrown all over the place).

There are two game modes: Challenge and SpeedRun, both available in four difficulty levels. Challenge is the standard game with a set amount of levels on the way to the dino sanctuary. SpeedRun is a mode that has individual levels which needs to be bought in any order using bones you collected during your game.

The multiplayer mode offers the ability to race up to 3 other players online on a certain course. Also there you can create a user and develop the stats of your own dinosaur.

422827.overview: Drop Dead is a series of ragdoll games developed by ttursas. It has 10 games in the series.

422829.overview: Double Wires is a simple 2D side-scrolling physics game. You control a ragdoll stick figure that can shoot adhesive wires out of each hand. These wires detach after a few seconds. Click inside the level to direct your wires onto the geometry of the level. Try to navigate your ragdoll body as far through the level as you can without falling off the bottom of the screen. Progress is measured in distance travelled.

422830.overview:
Drunken Masters is a bartender simulator flash game that was developed by Dan Hoelck and released on March 5, 2008.

In Drunken Masters, the player controls a bartender who works in a popular bar and must serve a large number of customers by mixing and making the drinks they request. Before the player starts the game, they can choose from ten characters to play as, each coming with unique stats. While the game will start off with customers only requesting simple drinks like beer, further into the game customers will request cocktails that require the player to mix a number of different types of alcohol.

Once a customer orders their drink, they have a patience meter that will immediately start to go down. The player has a limited number of VIP coupons that they can give to angry customers. However, if they use more than two in a single day, the player will have to start the day again. Customer’s impatience can be eased by performing tricks at the bar, such as bottle throwing, flipping, and catching. The better the player performs, the more money in tips they will earn.

422831.overview:
Demon Swield is an action fighting game developed by laFunk and published on Kongregate on May 22, 2017.

A heartbroken demon fights his way through the shadow realm.

422832.overview: Dicewars is a strategy title that is a combination of Risk-style mechanics with randomized dice rolls. Conquer territories by rolling all the dice on one parcel against an opponent. The highest total wins. Extra dice are randomly distributed based on the largest number of united territories. Instant replay is available after the game.

422834.overview:
In keeping with games such as Pick Up the Phone Booth and Die and You Have To Burn The Rope, this is another winner whose title spells out the only salient rule to keep in mind.

Every level (there are 15) begins with a happy little puppy in the middle of the screen, with an exit sign indicating its goal off to the left and a gigantic howitzer cannon on the right pointed at the puppy. Each level begins after the player clicks the mouse on the "start" prompt. Any player contact with the mouse following that sets off the howitzer's hair-trigger, obliterating all traces of the puppy and ending the game. If left unhampered by the player's interference, the puppy will in every case eventually make its way, however roundabout, to the goal on the left side. The game, however, will employ underhanded tricks in attempts to trick the player into intervening and, regrettably, shooting the puppy. Don't. Don't shoot the puppy.

422836.overview: Control Domo-Kun as you attempt to save the world from chaos!

422837.overview:
Doodle God is an addicting puzzle & world building game where players use logic and ingenuity to create the entire universe.
Starting with the basic elements of earth, wind, fire and air players can build a world filled with locomotives, Dragons, skyscrapers, Aliens and more. In Planet mode players will discover a challenging new way to develop the universe of their dreams.
As you create elements watch the world come to life as new combinations create new elements, life-forms and objects that propagate the planet's surface. But beware with great power comes great responsibility. Players need to be aware of unintended consequences like a zombie plague and other catastrophes! Test your divine knowledge and challenge your friends online with the new Tournament mode. Each time players successfully create a new item they’ll be rewarded with wit and wisdom from some of the greatest philosophers and comedians of all time. Unleash your inner god with Doodle God™ for Steam!

422838.overview:
Dragon Fist 3: Age of the Warrior is a fighting Flash game.

In this game, the player has to select a character and beat all of the other warriors in a melee fight.

422839.overview: A loving homage to Dragon's Lair and its FMV ilk, this game puts the player in control of "Guy" the stickman, imprisoned (for reasons left undiscussed) in a magical dungeon full of perilous traps and fantastical monsters. Guy needs to escape from it, and room by room he hopes to -- if only he can survive the lethal challenges awaiting him throughout the dungeon's every nook and cranny! Gameplay consists of clicking the mouse on briefly-indicated "hot spot"s -- quickly, lest a horrible fate befall Guy -- and then watching the animated outcome as Guy interacts with his sketchy stickman nightmare world. Three chances is all he gets before the player is obligated to start from the beginning again, but like its predecessors, gameplay is expanded by running through different portions of the dungeon randomly with every new run-through. The game is only completed, however, when every room has been survived.

422840.overview:
Drag Racer V3 is a drag racing Flash game developed by PhantomGames and released on April 8, 2004.

In this game, the player must control every aspect of their vehicle to try and attain high speeds on the drag strip. Typically, in most racing games, a player has to simply control the acceleration, put breaks, and turn, while in this game, the player has to additionally control the gas and gear shifting and time their gear changes well to gain the highest speeds.

422841.overview: Dig your way to the center of the earth in search for great treasures. Upgrade your equipment to help you along the way

422842.overview: Don't Escape is the first game of the Don't Escape series. It's a puzzle game that is basically a parody of escape room games, as the goal of this game is to interact with items in the room to make it so you can't escape. The player character is a werewolf, whose goal is to trap themselves in a cabin so that they do not kill anyone when the full moon rises and they shift into their beast form.

422843.overview:
Dark Cut is the first installment of Dark Cut series of games. It is developed by jmtb02 and it was released on November 15th, 2007 by Armor Games. It is preceded by Dark Cut 2 which was released on December 10th, 2007.

The setting of this game is the Middle Ages in Europe (according to history, names, and beliefs in-game). A player takes the role of a Humble Scholar (as suggested by the letters in the game), likely a trained physician of the time, tasked with performing various treatments from treating military wounds, routine pustule lancing, and even dispatching a Vampire.

422844.overview: Disorderly is an action, 2D keyboard-controlled Flash game developed by TomFulp (programmer) and Zeebarf (artist) and published on September 9, 2003. In this game, the goal of the player is to their job as an orderly in an old folk home by eliminating expensive elderly residents.

422847.overview:
Divine Intervention (Pt. 1) is the first Flash game Jim Bonacci made. It was released on October 23rd, 2003 on many websites including Newgrounds, Kongregate, and Total Jerkface. Divine Intervention is the only game other than Happy Wheels on Total Jerkface that Jim Bonacci has made so far.

The player is a priest in a small city that is being haunted by demons. He has been chosen by the Lord to get rid of them. First, a little possessed boy will charge at the priest, but by shooting it 3 times quickly enough, he will die and the priest can proceed. Then, a little possessed girl holding a sai in each hand will run up towards him and attempt to stab him, but same with the boy, shooting it 3 times will kill her. Afterwards, a possessed man will walk towards the priest and try to rip his arm off (or, if the arm got shot off, knock the priest down and crush his head). Shooting the man's torso or head 10 times or shooting both of his legs off with the shotgun (acquired later on) will kill him. Next, a friendly boy, possibly an alter server, is waving his hand and holding an uzi will say "Hey, over here! Look what I found! It can help you." When the priest walks up to him, he will automatically grab the gun. The player can actually choose to shoot him, but if done so, a huge "X" will flash and a buzzer will sound, telling the player that they should have not done that. However, this does not affect the story in any way.

In the next section, there will be a girl, a man, and a boy waiting for the priest. Walking close enough will make them spawn. After getting past them, there will be a new enemy, there is a circle with a rotating pentagram in it. When the priest walks close enough to it, an evil priest will appear. When he points at forward, he will use his laser attack that can be dodged by ducking. When he points at the ground, he will launch a "star" that will land and skim across the ground, which can be avoided by jumping over it. To kill the evil priest, the good priest must shoot off his shield, then shoot his body or head until he falls on his back. Next, there is another friendly boy who looks exactly like the boy who offered the priest the uzi. He is holding a shotgun and waving his hand. He will say the same quote he did when he found the uzi. However, a girl will run up to the priest and try to stab him if he walks too close.

The third section includes a man, a boy, and a girl. Even more boys and girls will spawn. Another evil priest will appear and do the same attacks he did in the last section.

The fourth section includes another man and the same boy and girl. Another evil priest will show up, but this will also make the boy appear unexpectedly. Afterwards, there is a trash can. When the priest walks up to it, a possessed old man will throw the lid and scream "DIIIIIIEEEEE oh my god.". If the priest doesn't duck under it, it will slice his head off.

422848.overview:
Demons vs Fairyland is a strategy tower defense Flash game developed by stormalligator and published on Kongregate on January 26, 2013.

In this game, the player can play as a group of fantasy characters who are defending against the inhabitants of Fairyland. They will have to build camps to prevent them from coming to take the kids.

The game features skeletons, beasts, zombies, enemies, 30 skills, 56 achievements, and tower upgrades with their special abilities.

422850.overview:
Dungeons of Kong is a dungeon RPG developed by nerdook and published on Kongregate on November 6, 2013.

An epic RPG starring Jim, Greg, Emily, Mojo and Nerdook! Assemble the ultimate team of heroes, each with their own set of skills, and delve into a randomly generated dungeon to destroy an Ancient Evil before it awakens!

422851.overview:
Duck Life 4 is the fourth installment in the Duck Life series, released on February 16th, 2012 on NotDoppler originally, then released for other websites to use on February 23rd, 2012.

Duck Life 4 takes place one year after the events of Duck Life 3: Evolution. At this time, genetically modified ducks are banned, and one duck racer reigns supreme. The player must travel across six different worlds to beat him.

440653.overview:
Demon Burst is an arcade action game made for "A Game by its Cover 2019" jam, inspired by games such as Kid Icarus, Castlevania and Ghosts 'n Goblins.

The game's concept and name were inspired by the original artwork of Philip Summers, made for the 2019 edition of My Famicase exhibition.

Game, Art & Sound by Crowno

482494.overview: Pilot a First World War biplane in a side-view arcade dogfight. Climb and dive to bring enemy aircraft into your line of fire while avoiding their attacks. Compact aerial encounters reward positioning behind a target rather than firing blindly ahead. The game mixes straightforward flight controls with the looping manoeuvres of an air duel.

482495.overview: Return to First World War aerial combat in a side-view arcade shooter. Manoeuvre a biplane around enemy aircraft, line up attacks and complete a succession of combat missions. Choosing the right angle of approach helps keep a target in range without exposing your own plane. The sequel expands the original Dogfight with a longer series of challenges.
